_about: Roasts keyed by normalized material family (#1651); the engine matches the print's material string to one family, most specific first.
_license: Original to Print Handy; AGPL-3.0-only with the project.

pla.text: {title} in PLA: the gateway filament, and the gateway is wide open again.
PLA again for {title}, because the classics never ask for an enclosure or forgiveness.
{title} chose the easygoing filament and still found a way to take {duration}.
Nothing says confidence like printing {title} in the filament everyone learned on.
{printer} and PLA go together like deadlines and suddenly urgent test prints.
{title} is PLA proof that simple materials still produce complicated shelf arrangements.

petg.text: {title} in PETG: stringing was invited, and it brought friends and a plus one.
PETG gave {title} toughness, shine, and a decorative fringe nobody sliced for.
{title} survived PETG, the filament that treats retraction as a polite suggestion.
With PETG, {title} is basically weatherproof, which the desk appreciates deeply.
{printer} printed {title} in PETG and only mildly resembled a candy floss machine.
PETG layers bond like family at holidays: strongly, permanently, and with some string attached.

tpu.text: {title} in TPU bends, squishes, and springs back, unlike anyone who tuned its retraction.
Flexible filament, flexible standards: {title} wobbles so nobody else has to.
{title} came out of TPU with the posture of a relaxed noodle at rest.
Printing TPU taught {printer} patience, humility, and the true meaning of slow extrusion.
{title} is TPU, so dropping it is now a feature demonstration, not an accident.
TPU gave {title} a bounce that its dignity will need time to recover from.

abs.text: {title} in ABS: the fumes were vintage, the warping was traditional, the finish is earned.
ABS made {title} the old way, with heat, attitude, and a closed door policy.
{printer} printed ABS for {title}, and the enclosure finally feels professionally needed.
{title} in ABS is tough enough to outlast the debate about printing ABS indoors.
ABS layer adhesion on {title} is strong, and so are the fumes, so crack a window.
Classic ABS behavior from {title}: stubborn during printing, dependable forever after.

asa.text: {title} in ASA is ready for sunshine, rain, and being left outside confidently.
ASA gave {title} a tan-proof future and a very outdoorsy sense of purpose.
{title} chose ASA, the filament that treats weather as a minor scheduling detail.
With ASA, {title} can live outside now, which frees up premium indoor shelf space.
{printer} made {title} in ASA, officially sun-rated and picnic-adjacent.
ASA on {title}: ultraviolet resistance outside, quiet smugness inside.

nylon.text: {title} in nylon is stronger than the excuses made for printing it this late.
Nylon kept {title} tough and the filament dryer gainfully employed all week.
{printer} printed nylon for {title}, a material that drinks moisture like gossip.
{title} in nylon could survive the toolbox, the truck, and a determined toddler.
Dry box hours were logged, tears were avoided, and nylon delivered {title} beautifully.
Nylon gave {title} engineering-grade confidence and hobby-grade drying requirements.

pc.text: {title} in polycarbonate: temperatures were high and so were everyone's expectations.
PC pushed {printer} to its thermal limits so {title} could shrug off almost anything.
{title} chose polycarbonate, the filament equivalent of bringing safety goggles to brunch.
With PC, {title} is heat-resistant, impact-resistant, and casually resistant to being replaced.
Printing PC for {title} turned the hotend into the hardest-working appliance here.
{title} in PC is overqualified for its job and intends to mention it often.

hips.text: {title} in HIPS, a material famous for supporting others, finally gets the lead role.
HIPS stepped out of the support act and into the spotlight with {title}.
{title} chose HIPS, proof that the understudy filament can carry a whole print.
{printer} gave HIPS top billing for {title}, and it dissolved nobody's expectations.
HIPS on {title}: smooth finish, hidden talents, and a faint citrus-based secret.
{title} in HIPS is the support material's solo album, and it holds up well.

wood.text: {title} in wood-fill smells like a workshop and sands like a tiny lumber project.
Wood filament gave {title} grain, warmth, and a legitimate reason to sand something.
{title} is part print, part carpentry, and entirely committed to the bit.
{printer} printed {title} with wood-fill, the closest thing to whittling by robot.
Wood-fill made {title} look hand-carved, assuming the hand owned excellent layer lines.
{title} in wood filament: now eligible for both shelf display and lumber jokes.

carbon.text: {title} in carbon-fiber filament looks fast even while sitting perfectly still.
Carbon fill gave {title} racing stripes in its soul and abrasiveness in its nozzle history.
{title} chose carbon composite, because regular plastic lacked sufficient motorsport energy.
{printer} survived carbon filament for {title}, and the brass nozzle sends its regards.
Carbon-fiber {title}: stiffer, darker, and legally required to look slightly tactical.
With carbon fill, {title} weighs less and implies considerably more lap time.
